sentences.text:
This miscellaneous appeal has been filed by the appellant/insurance company under Section 173(1)
of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 , being aggrieved by the Award dated 29.11.2016 passed by Member,
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Guna (M.P.) (in short "the Claims Tribunal") in Claim Case No.41/2012 seeking exoneration of insurance company from its liability.

entities.text: Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, District- Guna (M.P.)
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. The date of the accident and the issue of negligence are not in dispute; however, the dispute pertains only to the liability.
3.

As per the findings recorded by the Claims Tribunal in the case of injury sustained by the claimant due to the motor accident, the Claims Tribunal has awarded compensation to the tune of Rs.2,05,600/- along with interest.
NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-GWL:4449 2 MA-174-2017 4.

Learned counsel for the appellant has filed the present appeal on the ground that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle was holding a valid and effective driving licence for a light motor vehicle (LMV), and the driving licence was not endorsed to permit him to drive a The Oriental Insurance Co. 1 transport/commercial vehicle as well as at the time of alleged accident, owner of the offending vehicle did not possess valid and effective permit.

sentences.text:
Therefore, it is contended that the Claims Tribunal has committed an error in imposing liability upon the Insurance Company, and accordingly, setting aside of the impugned award against the Insurance Company is sought.
5.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the respondent No.1 opposed the prayer and prayed for dismissal of the appeal.

6. Heard the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
7.

It is not disputed that at the time of the accident, the driver of the offending vehicle i.e. Magic bearing registration No. MP 08 T 1590 was holding a licence to drive a light motor vehicle and the claimant was third party.
It is also not disputed that at the time of the accident, he was driving the offending vehicle, the weight of of offending vehicle was 990 kgs which is less than 7,500 kgs.

8. In this regard, reliance can be placed upon the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2017 SC 3668, wherein the Apex Court has held as under:
"(ii) A transport vehicle and omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7,500 kg, would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, the 'unladen weight' of which does not exceed NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-GWL:4449 3 MA-174-2017 7,500 kg; and the holder of a driving licence to drive the class of 'light motor vehicle' as provided in Section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus, the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 kg."
9.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., AIR 2017 SC 3668
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is undisputed that at the time of alleged accident, the claimant was a third party.

In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co.
Ltd. , 2019 (2) MPLJ (SC) 8, and National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma and others,
2004 ACJ 2094, even if the offending vehicle is operated without a valid and effective permit, the insurance company is liable to pay the compensation to the claimant in the first instance and thereafter recover the same from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: 10. In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Mukund Dewangan (supra) and Amrit Paul (supra) , this Court does not find any substance on merits.
The Claims Tribunal has rightly held the Insurance Company to pay the compensation to the claimant and thereafter, recover the same from owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
Accordingly, no interference is warranted in the impugned award passed by the Claims Tribunal.
11. In view of the foregoing discussion, the instant miscellaneous appeal fails and is hereby dismissed.

(HIRDESH) JUDGE *VJ*

In view of the judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Amrit Paul Singh vs. TATA AIG General Insurance Co.
